\section{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- Small Set Expansion}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.SmallSetExpansion
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- Small Set Expansion: Introduction}
Indicators on the uniform Boolean cube satisfy moment identities and volume bounds. Two-function hypercontractivity gives a parameterized two-set expansion inequality and a one-set stability estimate.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- Small Set Expansion: Results}

\begin{definition}[Boolean-cube set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b001
}
For a set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, define $\mathbf1_A(x)=1$ if $x\in A$ and $\mathbf1_A(x)=0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform set volume]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b001
}
For a set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, define its volume $\mu(A)=\mathbb E_x\mathbf1_A(x)=|A|/2^n$ under the uniform cube law.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of a finite-set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
For any dimension $n\in\mathbb N$, any finite subset $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, and any
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the indicator satisfies $0\le\mathbf 1_A(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Upper bound for a finite-set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
For any dimension $n\in\mathbb N$, any finite subset $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, and any
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the indicator satisfies $\mathbf 1_A(x)\le 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute value of a set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.abs_setIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator_nonneg}
\difficulty{1}
For a finite set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ and a point $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the indicator
satisfies $|\mathbf 1_A(x)|=\mathbf 1_A(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Idempotence of a finite-set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
For any dimension $n\in\mathbb N$, finite subset $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, and point
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, one has $\mathbf 1_A(x)^2=\mathbf 1_A(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positive powers of a finite-set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
For any dimension $n\in\mathbb N$, finite subset $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, point
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and real number $r>0$, one has $\mathbf 1_A(x)^r=\mathbf 1_A(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positive powers of a set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.abs_setIndicator_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.abs_setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator_rpow}
\difficulty{3}
For a finite set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, a point $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and a real number
$r>0$, the indicator satisfies $|\mathbf 1_A(x)|^r=\mathbf 1_A(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute moment of a set indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_indicator_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.abs_setIndicator_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a subset of the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube and let $r>0$. Under the uniform
measure, the expectation of the $r$th power of the absolute value of its indicator is
equal to the volume of $A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator moment norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_Lr_norm}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_indicator_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ and let $r\in\mathbb R$ with $r>0$. Under the uniform
probability measure on the Boolean cube, the $r$-moment norm of its indicator is
$\bigl(\mathbb E|\mathbf1_A|^r\bigr)^{1/r}=\mu(A)^{1/r}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegative uniform volume]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and every set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, the uniform volume
$\mu(A)$ satisfies $0\le\mu(A)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform volume upper bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, the uniform volume
$\mu(A)$ satisfies $\mu(A)\le1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Parameterized two-set expansion]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.generalized_small_set_expansion}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_indicator_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.general_two_function_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p260-b005}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A,B\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ have uniform volumes $\alpha,\beta$, and let real $p,u,\rho$ satisfy $1\le p\le u$, $u\ge2$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho\le\sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$. Then $\mathbb E[\mathbf1_AT_\rho\mathbf1_B]\le\alpha^{(u-1)/u}\beta^{1/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-set noise stability bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.small_set_expansion}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.generalized_small_set_expansion, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p254-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p254-b006
}
\difficulty{4}
For every $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ of uniform volume $\alpha$ and $0<\rho\le1$, $\mathbb E[\mathbf1_AT_\rho\mathbf1_A]\le\alpha^{2/(1+\rho)}$.
\end{theorem}
